newsitem.title: GERMANY: Soybean buyers seen confident of 1997 supply.
newsitem.headline: Soybean buyers seen confident of 1997 supply.

text.p: Importers who recently ordered soybeans from the U.S. may now stop buying as Latin American new crops flow onto the market, the Oil World newsletter said on Tuesday.
The independent publication said consumers were increasingly confident of ample supply this year and might prefer to draw down stocks.
Brazil's export performance in early 1997 had by far exceeded earlier expectations as the impact of port strikes was more than offset by improvements in transport and port facilities, it said.
Brazilian exports in February/April 1997 totalled 2.32 million tonnes versus 1.12 million in the same 1996 period.
Net exports from the U.S. in that period rose to 6.29 million tonnes from 6.27 million a year earlier as customers covered against the possibility of serious disruption in Brazil, Oil World said.
That no longer appeared necessary, which should narrow the price premium of old crop over new crop soybeans.
Global demand was easing and South American sellers were marketing aggressively.
